text:
maria: Heads-up: after the merge of PR#4207 to main we see a ~12% p95 token latency regression on int8 profiles in staging. Only on longer sequences (>512 tokens). Telemetry: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/2239 - looks consistent across two different GPU types.

aj: noticed that too. CI perf job flagged it earlier this morning but I dismissed as noise. Can you paste perf graph?

maria: pasted the screenshot in thread + link. The flamegraph points to more time in dequant + memcpy hotloop. nvprof shows extra memcpy from kernel-selection fallback.

kai: hmm - PR4207 touched the kernel selector table (added a normalization key for shape tolerance). Could that change cache key ordering?

maria: that's my hunch. The selector is hitting a fallback path that does a shape-normalize-and-copy before running optimized int8 kernel. Before the change it hit the fast path.

olivia: Any repro steps? I can try a quick bisect if we have a deterministic perf test.

maria: repro: run perf/regression/int8_longseq on p3.2xlarge image with the quantized gpt-like model: 
```bash
# local repro
PYTHONPATH=./python ./bench/run_latency.py --model quantized-gpt-7B --dtype int8 --seq_len 1024 --batch 1
```
You should see p95 increase from ~120ms -> ~135ms after merge branch.

aj: I'll start a git bisect on the perf harness between v1.2.3 (good) and main (bad).

perf-bot: CI perf alert: job=perf/int8_longseq p95 delta +11.8% (sig=2.9), triggered at 2026-03-18T09:12:04Z

kai: I instrumented the selector quickly: new normalization adds an ordering step which mutates the key tuple; sometimes it adds a dtype flag at a different position. It's plausible the hash changed so caches miss and fall back.

aj: bisect step 1: PR 4195..4210 range. Running 12 tests, will update.

maria: another data point: KV cache telemetry shows higher miss rate during the long-seq runs. Suspect the extra memcpy happens when we normalize cache layout for the fallback kernel.

olivia: If it's cache-key ordering, a quick revert to old key layout in selector should restore perf. Can we hotfix?

aj: bisect landed on PR#4207 as the first bad commit (confirmed locally). Confirming with CI runs now.

perf-bot: Bisect result: culprit commit 4207a1d - "selector: normalize tensor key for stable matching". Reproduced on perf runner.

maria: confirmed on staging profiler: commit 4207a1d increases memcpy-bytes by ~20MB per request on longer sequences. That's the extra 10-12% latency.

kai: ok patch idea: keep the normalization but ensure ordering and dtype position are stable and don't change backward compatibility of cache keys. Also add a versioned key prefix to selector so future changes are explicit.

olivia: can we ship a rollback first to restore SLA on canaries? deploy-bot, status?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for main at 02:03 UTC due to p95 regression monitor. Auto-rollback not enabled.

aj: I'm opening PR#4216 with a minimal revert of the normalization change to restore previous key generation. Also adding a unit test that validates cache-key stability across shapes and dtype permutations.

maria: sound plan. Meanwhile, I'll add a perf-test to post-merge gate so CI catches this before canary.

kai: after PR4216 we should also add a telemetry metric: selector_key_version so we can detect future silent key churn.

olivia: action items: 
- aj: land PR4216 (revert) + unit tests
- maria: add perf gate to post-merge CI
- kai: follow-up PR to add versioned key and guard rails
- ops: hold canary until PR4216 merges and passes staging perf

aj: PR4216 created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4216 - running internal CI now.

maria: CI perf job just finished on PR4216: p95 delta -0.4% vs v1.2.3 (within noise). Staging load tests look back to normal.

perf-bot: CI perf for PR4216: p95 delta -0.2% (not significant).

olivia: great. Landing on my go. I'll coordinate a canary resume once merged and we see stable runs for 30m.

kai: follow-up: I'll draft the selector_key_version change and a short doc in the repo about compatibility expectations for kernel selector keys.

maria: thanks team. Learned: even small deterministic changes to selector key shape can silently change runtime behavior via cache misses -> memcpys. We should treat selector key as a public contract within runtime (test + telemetry). :white_check_mark:
